subject: Brightlane mutual action plan — performance runbook, access windows, and TTFT results
messages:
From: Jane Morris <jane.morris@brightlane.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan & perf run — initial ask

Hi Rafael (and team),

Thanks again for the demo last week. Brightlane is ready to move to a brief, focused MAP to validate Redwood in our staging workload and ensure we can meet our latency and TTFT targets before closing. High-level asks: 

- Validate TTFT (time-to-first-token) and p95 response latency for 512-token generations at our expected concurrency
- Confirm scalable throughput at sustained 200 req/s and burst to 1k req/s for 5-minute windows
- Verify prefix caching behavior for repeated prompt families and measure any cold-starts
- Provide a short mutual action plan (owners, dates, access required) and a benchmarking window we can commit to

We can provide two staging clusters (stg-east and stg-west) and a small set of test accounts. Preferred window next week: Dec 3–4 (US morning). Procurement and infra cc'd for keys and procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Morris
Head of Platform Engineering — Brightlane
[jane.morris@brightlane.com]

[Attachment: initial_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Morris <jane.morris@brightlane.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf run — proposed MAP and schedule

Jane — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short MAP and a recommended benchmarking runbook attached (Brightlane_MAP_v1.xlsx). Highlights here so we can align quickly: 

1) Owners and dates
   - Redwood: Rafael Mendes (PM) — overall owner; Marissa Cole — benchmark engineering lead; Karthik Iyer — runtime tuning
   - Brightlane: Jane Morris (platform owner); Brightlane Infra (infra lead)
   - Proposed windows: Dec 3 (prep + smoke), Dec 4 (full runs), fallback Dec 6 if needed

2) Test targets
   - TTFT target: <= 400 ms p50, <= 700 ms p95 for 512-token responses at steady-state
   - Throughput: sustain 200 req/s for 30m, bursts to 1k req/s for 5m
   - Concurrency: simulate 300 concurrent sessions with variable token lengths (128/256/512)

3) Logistics (access) — action items for Brightlane infra:
   - Provide staging endpoint URLs and a set of 5 test API keys scoped to the staging project
   - Whitelist Redwood IP ranges (we will provide) and enable test accounts by Dec 2 EOD

4) Artifacts we will deliver
   - Runbook (attached)
   - Raw benchmark CSV + condensed results summary post-run
   - Suggested runtime tuning (batch sizes, KV cache TTL)

I've attached the MAP and a runbook. Marissa — can you add the load generator configuration and the exact traffic schedule in the sheet? Karthik — I'll defer to you for any quick quant/quantization changes if we need to trade cost vs latency.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Brightlane_MAP_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Morris <jane.morris@brightlane.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf run — load config and keys (internal + external)

Looping in details for the load window and what we need from Brightlane infra. Copying the text I sent to infra for transparency: 

— Test endpoints:
  • stg-east.redwood-infer.brightlane:443 (primary)
  • stg-west.redwood-infer.brightlane:443 (failover)

— Test accounts/keys (we need from Brightlane):
  • 5 API keys (scoped to staging project, TTL 14 days). Requesting these be created as: bl-test-01..bl-test-05
  • One read-only admin user to fetch logs (for post-mortem tracing)

— Load generator config (we will push to the runbook sheet):
  • Workload mix: 60% 256-token, 30% 512-token, 10% 128-token
  • Ramp: 5m linear ramp to 200 req/s, hold 30m, 1m ramp to 1k for 5m bursts, cool down 10m
  • Concurrency simulation: 300 sessions with KV cache priming sequence for 20% of sessions

— Security note:
  • Please confirm encrypted key delivery channel (preferred: S3 presigned link or secure DocuSign envelope for signatures). Do not send keys over plain email.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Benchmarking Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: test-keys-stub.txt (text/plain) — placeholder for key names]

From: Jane Morris <jane.morris@brightlane.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightlane Infra <infra@brightlane.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf run — load config and keys (confirming window)

Rafael / Marissa — thanks, this looks good. Infra will create the five keys (bl-test-01..05) and send an S3 presigned link for key pickup by EOD Dec 2 (they slipped; will be by Dec 3 morning PST). Procurement flagged a quick PO approval that should be done on Dec 3.

We can confirm Dec 4 for the full run: start at 09:00 PST (stg-east) with the schedule you proposed. If you need a second set of runs in the evening (to observe different cluster load), we can do a 18:00 PST run as a follow-up.

Also calling out a hard requirement from our compliance team: all benchmark logs must be retained for 90 days and we need a signed attestation documenting that benchmark traffic was only run against staging clusters. Can Redwood provide a short post-run attestation?

Jane
Jane Morris
Head of Platform Engineering — Brightlane

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Morris <jane.morris@brightlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf run — results and next steps

Jane — appreciate the team moving fast. We completed the Dec 4 09:00 PST full run and the evening follow-up at 18:00 PST. Attached are the raw results CSV and the final MAP workbook with annotations. TL;DR results summary: 

- TTFT (512 tokens): p50 = 360 ms, p95 = 690 ms (meets p50 target; p95 is marginally above 700 ms target on the evening run due to node contention)
- Response latency (all sizes): p50 = 280 ms, p95 = 620 ms
- Sustained throughput: 220 req/s sustained for 30m (slightly above the target)
- Burst behavior: successfully hit 1k req/s for 4m 30s; when bursts exceeded 1k for >5m we observed queueing and a ~3% error rate (timeouts)
- Concurrency: simulated 300 sessions with KV cache priming — cache hit rate during steady-state was ~72%
- Failures: total 3.1% of requests errored during the highest evening burst; root cause tied to a transient autoscaling lag on the customer staging cluster (Brightlane infra warmed slower than expected)

Action items and recommendations: 
1) Redwood will provide a post-run attestation and 90-day log retention statement (attached).
2) We recommend a tuning pass on autoscaling thresholds and increase of short-lived warm pool for burst windows — Karthik to propose exact params in 48 hours.
3) If Brightlane is comfortable with the marginal p95 deviation in one window, we can move to a commercial close and start transfer to Dedicated capacity with an agreed SLA.

Please find the artifacts attached: benchmark_results_brightlane_20261205.csv and updated Brightlane_MAP_v1.xlsx (annotated).

Next steps: Rafael will coordinate a short exec sync to close — propose Dec 9 or Dec 10 for a 30-min alignment with procurement and platform execs.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
